children.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, investigate OpenMP parallelization of the independent coarse-root tile traversal, passing the run() threads argument through so it is an upper bound on the team size. The current tree update must complete before root shading begins; each root must write only its own pixels. Compare scheduling choices for the uneven work among roots, avoid needless parallel overhead at one thread, and preserve the existing shading and culling behavior. Validate correctness, full output writes, and performance at both 1 and 4 cores, including altered light colors.
children.subject: Parallelize independent coarse tiles within the requested thread budget

children.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, investigate reducing work in MinMaxZTree and the conservative light-culling/recursive traversal path (including SplitTileMinMax and IntersectLightsWithTileMinMax). Measure tradeoffs among hierarchy granularity, culling work, and false-positive light lists; any changed bounds or culling must remain conservative and never discard a contributing light. Recompute bounds from the current depth buffer on every invocation, do not cache rendered results, and retain a correct path for dimensions not supported by a chosen tile layout. Keep this branch focused on culling/hierarchy rather than adding parallelism or changing the shading kernel; validate both core counts and altered light colors.
children.subject: Reduce recursive hierarchy and conservative light-culling overhead

children.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, focus on ShadeTileC's per-pixel BRDF evaluation: investigate safe reuse of pixel and light values, reducing expensive normalization/pow work, and/or row-wise compiler vectorization. Preserve the original shading semantics closely; any approximation must meet the one-intensity-level tolerance on all correctness checks, including altered light colors, and must not rely on a single expected frame. Do not change the tile-culling strategy or introduce threading in this branch; measure both 1- and 4-core cases and retain a portable path unless the frozen build proves a specific ISA is available.
children.subject: Optimize per-pixel shading math and row-wise vectorization
